title: India's Boxers Make CWG History With Record 10 Guaranteed Medals in Glasgow
excerpt: Every Indian semifinalist won their bout as the boxing squad shattered the country's previous best of nine medals at a single Commonwealth Games.
body:
• All 10 Indian boxers — seven women and three men — won their semifinal bouts, guaranteeing a record 10 medals and surpassing the previous best of nine from the 2018 Gold Coast Games
  • Jaismine Lamboria, Lovlina Borgohain, Preeti Pawar, and Priya Ghanghas lead a dominant women's squad with finalists across multiple weight classes
  • India's overall CWG medal count stands at 23 (5 gold, 12 silver, 6 bronze) with boxing contributing the most medals of any sport
  • The finals are scheduled for August 1-2, with India targeting all 10 gold medals

A Perfect 10 in the Ring

India's boxing contingent wrote a new chapter in Commonwealth Games history on Thursday, guaranteeing a record 10 medals after every single semifinalist won their bout in Glasgow. The achievement shattered the previous CWG boxing record of nine medals set at the 2018 Gold Coast Games and surpassed the seven medals won in Birmingham four years ago.

https://x.com/DDNewslive/status/2083371385896808488

The milestone is remarkable not just for its scale but for its completeness. India entered 14 boxers — seven women and seven men — and 10 of them reached the semifinals, where a loss still guarantees bronze. All 10 converted. The four who fell in earlier rounds were narrowly edged out in a competition that featured 201 boxers from 43 nations.

Women's Squad Leads the Charge

The women's team has been the backbone of India's campaign. Jaismine Lamboria, the reigning world champion at 57kg and world No. 1, powered through her semifinal after arriving in Glasgow in peak form from her 2025 World Championships gold in Liverpool. Sakshi Choudhary, who earned her spot on the team by defeating world champions Nikhat Zareen and Minakshi Hooda at national trials, delivered a composed performance at 51kg.

Lovlina Borgohain, the Tokyo Olympics bronze medallist, received a walkover into the semis in the 75kg category and is chasing her first-ever Commonwealth Games medal despite being one of India's most decorated boxers internationally. Arundhati Choudhary's run at 70kg has been especially gutsy — she revealed she had to shed nearly two kilograms in a single day to make weight before her bout.

"Boxing is once again expected to contribute significantly to India's medal tally despite the Commonwealth Games programme being reduced to just 10 sports this year."

— MyKhel

Preeti Pawar (54kg), fresh off gold medals at both the Grand Prix in Czechia and the Asian Boxing Championships in Mongolia, and Priya Ghanghas (60kg) round out the women's finalists. Parveen Hooda (65kg) fell just short in her quarterfinal.

Young Men's Squad Steps Up

On the men's side, India sent a youthful squad with six of seven boxers making their CWG debut. Sachin Siwach, a former World Youth Champion, lived up to his billing as India's strongest men's medal contender with a commanding 5-0 quarterfinal victory in the 60kg class. Ankush dominated at 80kg with another unanimous decision, while heavyweight Narender Berwal edged Samoa's Michael Seko in a tight 3-2 split decision to reach the +90kg last four.

Jadumani Singh (55kg) had already secured his semifinal berth earlier in the week, while Aditya Pratap Singh (65kg), Sumit Kundu (70kg), and Kapil Pokhariya (90kg) were eliminated in their respective weight categories.

India's Broader CWG Campaign

Boxing's dominance has been crucial for India's overall standing at the 2026 Games, where the country has accumulated 23 medals — five gold, 12 silver, and six bronze — across 10 sports. With the boxing finals spread across August 1-2, India's pugilists have a realistic shot at converting several of these guaranteed medals into gold, which would significantly boost the nation's final standing in Glasgow.

Head coach Santiago Nieva has expressed confidence that the women's team can match or surpass its Birmingham 2022 performance, where India won two gold medals and one bronze. Given the current form, that target looks conservative.
